exam_metadata.subject_name: Creativity Mindset for Innovation and Imagination

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the role of creativity in education?

options.A: Preparing students only for existing jobs.
options.B: Focusing on memorization skills.
options.C: Equipping students to face future challenges and unknown careers.

questions.question_text: What is the first thing that machines took away from humans according to the above lecture?

options.B: Memory

questions.question_text: How does love serve as a driver of creativity ?

options.A: It pushes people to take on tasks they fear
options.B: It allows individuals to tolerate fear, greed, and duty while pursuing what they enjoy
options.C: It encourages people to work solely for recognition and rewards
options.D: It removes the need for discipline in creative tasks

questions.question_text: What is the first step towards being creative?

options.B: Taking care of your mental, emotional, and physical well-being
options.D: Learning as many skills as possible

questions.question_text: What is the key takeaway from the story involving Bill Gates and Warren Buffett ?

options.B: Focus is the secret to success
options.C: Creativity is a matter of genetics
options.D: Collaboration is the most important factor in success

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between intelligence and creativity as described in the document?

options.A: More intelligent people are always more creative.
options.B: Creativity is unrelated to intelligence.
options.C: More intelligent people tend to be more creative but must break established patterns.
options.D: Less intelligent people are more creative because they don't rely on patterns.

questions.question_text: Why does the brain rely on System 1 thinking for most daily tasks?

options.A: System 1 is more reliable and accurate
options.B: System 1 helps conserve mental energy by using patterns
options.C: System 1 is used to solve complex problems
options.D: System 1 is error-free and faster at decision-making

questions.question_text: What does a T-shaped personality refer to?

options.A: Someone who has no depth in any specific area but knows a little about everything.
options.B: Someone with deep domain expertise and a wide breadth of perspective.
options.C: Someone who focuses solely on one profession without any other affiliations.
options.D: Someone who only has a basic understanding of multiple subjects.

questions.question_text: What lesson can be learned from Thomas Edison's approach to creating the light bulb?

options.A: Failure is a waste of time and should be avoided
options.B: Failure provides valuable lessons and is part of the experimental process
options.C: Only a single attempt should be made to avoid wasting resources

questions.question_text: What does it mean to take 'Half Chances' according to the document?

options.A: Waiting for the perfect opportunity to arise
options.B: Avoiding risks and waiting for approval
options.C: Relying on others to present you with the ideal opportunity
options.D: Grabbing opportunities even if they aren't fully formed

questions.question_text: What does Angela Duckworth's concept of "grit" emphasize in her book?

options.B: Persistence and effort are key to achieving success
options.C: Creativity does not require any effort
options.D: Grit is only about hard work, without the need for experimentation

questions.question_text: Why does Albert Einstein believe imagination is more important than knowledge?

options.A: Imagination is easier to acquire than knowledge
options.B: Knowledge explains what has happened, while imagination can predict what could happen
options.C: Knowledge limits creativity, while imagination leads to hard work
options.D: Knowledge is essential for problem-solving, while imagination is not

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between a symptom and a problem?

options.A: Symptoms are the same as problems
options.B: Symptoms are surface-level issues, while problems are deeper, root causes
options.D: Problems are more frequent than symptoms

questions.question_text: In the example of the Bangalore traffic problem, what did the person solve instead of the traffic issue?

options.B: He solved the problem of time wastage
options.C: He found a shortcut to avoid traffic

questions.question_text: What happens when you expand your "zone of influence"?

options.A: You become more concerned about various issues
options.B: You are able to change the world through problem-solving
options.D: You become more stressed about things you cannot control

questions.question_text: In the 5 Whys technique, what is the main purpose of asking "Why" multiple times?

options.B: To discover the root cause of a problem
options.D: To understand only the surface-level issues

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the Fishbone Diagram?

options.A: To find only one cause of a problem
options.B: To brainstorm all possible solutions
options.C: To visually map out the causes of a problem in categories
options.D: To explore the consequences of decisions

questions.question_text: What is a stakeholder in the context of problem exploration?

options.A: A person who directly solves the problem
options.B: An individual or group influencing or affected by the problem

questions.question_text: What does the MECE principle stand for in problem prioritization?

options.B: Mutually Exclusive, Collectively Exhaustive

questions.question_text: Which of the following are types of empathy as described in the above session? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Compassionate Empathy

questions.question_text: What role do constraints play in problem framing?

options.A: They limit creativity and make problem-solving harder
options.B: They help to define non-negotiable boundaries that guide creativity
options.C: They are optional and unnecessary in most problems
options.D: They remove the need for creativity in problem-solving

questions.question_text: Which of the following are part of the FAB model? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Functions

questions.question_text: What is the key benefit of allowing participants to generate more ideas during ideation?

options.A: They will create fewer average ideas
options.B: It helps improve the quality of ideas over time
options.C: It avoids confusion and makes selection easy
options.D: It reduces the number of ideas to select from

questions.question_text: What is the core principle of the "Challenging Assumptions" ideation method?

options.B: Questioning existing beliefs to unlock new possibilities

questions.question_text: What does 'lateral thinking' mean in the context of ideation?

options.B: Thinking in a structured, linear way
options.C: Taking an unconventional, sideways approach to problem-solving

questions.question_text: What does the 'S' in SCAMPER stand for?

options.B: Substitute

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of ideation triggers?

options.B: To stimulate creative thinking and explore new industries or markets

questions.question_text: What is a common reason for 'Refusing' users to not adopt a product?

options.B: High product cost

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the value levers in the buyer utility map?

options.B: Simplicity

questions.question_text: What is the primary focus of the Theory of Constraints (TOC)?

options.B: Identifying and managing the bottlenecks in a system

questions.question_text: What are the three levels in the Nine Windows method?

options.B: Individual, Group, and Society

questions.question_text: Where did Toyota get the idea for its 'Just-In-Time' inventory system?

options.B: Ford Motor Company

questions.question_text: What feature was originally designed for visually impaired people but benefits all users?

options.B: Subtitles in movies

questions.question_text: Which three criteria must be combined for an idea to be considered a winning one?

options.A: Creativity, originality, and speed of implementation
options.B: Financial investment, technical expertise, and customer interest
options.C: Time efficiency, cost reduction, and innovation
options.D: Human desirability, technical feasibility, and business viability
